Elena —

Thanks for the details and for sharing the spike log. Were aligned on keeping p50 as a low-latency target and being pragmatic on p95 for bursty workloads. Id like to propose a compromise that weve validated internally: a dual-window measurement approach. High level:

- p50: rolling 1-minute window (captures short-tail latency consistently)
- p95: rolling 15-minute window with a timeboxed hourly carveout option for documented bursts (we can escalate to a 1-hour aggregation when burst detected)

Key benefits: preserves low-latency experience for interactive flows (p50) while giving predictable accounting for transient system-wide burst events (p95). Exceptions would be explicitly timeboxed (e.g., the hour of the spike) and require documented evidence (request + logs).

Ive looped in Ben (sales engineering) to attach a short tech note that explains measurement semantics and observability hooks; Irene will scope how this maps to our SLA appendix and the sample contract language.

If this sounds workable, we can draft the redline and run it by Legal.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Adding the tech perspective. Short answers first: yes, we can implement dual-window reporting; yes, we can timebox carveouts; yes, we can require evidence for each carveout (logs + prefix cache stats).

Notes in the attached PDF:
- Measurement plan: p50 = 1m rolling, p95 = 15m rolling with an optional elevated-hour aggregation for documented burst events (our telemetry flags a burst when qps exceeds a 5x baseline sustained >10 minutes).
- Impact on billing/credits: carveouts would be excluded from SLA breach calculations but not from metering/billing (so usage charge stays the same). For good governance we require a one-time notification and post-mortem within 72 hours.
- Observability hooks: we will publish a dedicated metric redwood.slo.burst_flag and a signed evidence bundle link for the hour in question.
